variations.name: Carbon credit registries (legacy standards bodies & next-gen digital registries)
variations.description: Standards bodies set crediting methodologies and run the registries where credits are issued, tracked and retired — the foundational ledger of integrity for the entire market.

companies.name: Verra
companies.what: Runs the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), the world's largest VCM crediting program and registry
companies.signal: 2,300+ projects, 1.2B+ tonnes issued; rebuilding trust after 2023 REDD+ over-crediting scandals; CCP-eligible

companies.name: Gold Standard
companies.what: Swiss nonprofit standard emphasizing SDG co-benefits; overhauled its assurance model in 2024
companies.signal: ICVCM CCP-eligible; widely used for cookstove/community projects and Article 6 pilots

companies.name: ACR (American Carbon Registry)
companies.what: First private voluntary GHG registry (founded 1996); strong in US industrial/IFM methodologies
companies.signal: ICVCM CCP-eligible program; registry tech historically powered by APX

companies.name: Climate Action Reserve
companies.what: North America-focused offset registry whose protocols seeded California's compliance program
companies.signal: ICVCM CCP-eligible; expanding into Mexico and soil enrichment protocols

companies.name: ART (Architecture for REDD+ Transactions)
companies.what: Jurisdictional REDD+ standard (TREES) crediting whole countries/states rather than projects
companies.signal: CCP-eligible; the standard behind the LEAF Coalition's sovereign forest deals

companies.name: Puro.earth
companies.what: First registry dedicated to engineered carbon removal (biochar, BECCS, mineralized carbon)
companies.signal: Majority-owned by Nasdaq since 2021; confirmed CCP-eligible by ICVCM in 2025

companies.name: Isometric
companies.what: Science-first digital registry for durable (1,000-year) CDR with in-house scientific review and free-to-buyer model
companies.signal: $25M seed (Lowercarbon, Plural, 2023); first registry endorsed by ICROA, CORSIA and ICVCM; used by Frontier/Google buyers

companies.name: Equitable Earth
companies.what: New community-centered REDD+/forest standard built to fix benefit-sharing flaws of legacy REDD
companies.signal: Achieved ICVCM CCP-eligibility in 2025 alongside the legacy programs

companies.name: International Carbon Registry (ICR)
companies.what: Iceland-based all-digital registry platform serving independent crediting programs and national pilots
companies.signal: Approved SustainCERT as VVB in Feb 2025; growing methodology catalog

companies.name: Global Carbon Council
companies.what: Qatar-based (GORD) crediting program focused on Global South energy and industrial projects
companies.signal: CORSIA-approved program; positioning for Article 6 host-country supply

variations.name: Spot/futures exchanges, marketplaces & brokerage desks
variations.description: Exchanges and brokers provide price discovery, standardized contracts and execution for carbon credits and allowances — compliance futures venues are deep and liquid while VCM spot venues are consolidating after the 2022-23 integrity crisis.

companies.name: Xpansiv (CBL)
companies.what: Operates CBL, the largest spot exchange for voluntary credits, plus IATA's Aviation Carbon Exchange and market data (XSignals); also owns APX registry infrastructure
companies.signal: Blackstone-backed ($400M, 2022); launched CBL GEO CORSIA Phase 1 spot contract April 2025

companies.name: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)
companies.what: Dominant venue for compliance carbon futures (EUA, UKA, California CCA, RGGI) plus VCM futures
companies.signal: Hosts the bulk of the ~€700B+/yr traded EU carbon derivatives market

companies.name: CME Group
companies.what: Lists GEO/N-GEO voluntary carbon futures and North American compliance contracts via NYMEX
companies.signal: VCM futures volumes fell sharply post-2022 but compliance complex remains active

companies.name: ACX (AirCarbon Exchange)
companies.what: Digital carbon exchange using commodity-trading architecture; first fully regulated carbon exchange and clearing house (ADGM, Abu Dhabi)
companies.signal: Cited among major platforms in 2025 market studies; Abu Dhabi and Singapore operations

companies.name: Climate Impact X (CIX)
companies.what: Singapore exchange/marketplace running auctions, standardized contracts and CIX Intelligence price benchmarks
companies.signal: Backed by Temasek, DBS, SGX and Standard Chartered; still operating in 2025 despite thin VCM volumes

companies.name: STX Group
companies.what: Amsterdam-based environmental commodities trader and brokerage spanning VCM, biofuels, RECs and ETS (owns broker Vertis)
companies.signal: Cut staff in 2024-25 amid VCM slowdown but refinanced a €290M borrowing-base facility; executed >$1B US tax-credit transfer

companies.name: Carbon Trade Exchange (CTX)
companies.what: Long-running electronic spot exchange for voluntary credits with direct registry integrations
companies.signal: Operating since 2009 but low public traction signals in 2024-26

variations.name: API-based credit retail & embedded offsetting for consumer apps
variations.description: API platforms let any company embed credit purchase and retirement into checkout flows, travel bookings or fintech products, aggregating small-ticket demand that registries were never built to serve.

companies.name: Patch
companies.what: Started as the offset API; now a full platform for sourcing, buying and managing credit portfolios
companies.signal: $55M Series B; relaunched enterprise procurement platform in April 2025

companies.name: Cloverly
companies.what: API pioneer (Southern Company spinout) now also selling commerce software to carbon project developers; powers Salesforce's marketplace
companies.signal: $19M Series A (2023); 200+ enterprise customers

companies.name: Lune
companies.what: London API embedding emission calculations plus vetted credits into fintech, logistics and payments products
companies.signal: Seed-funded (2022); clients across European fintech/logistics

companies.name: Chooose
companies.what: Oslo platform powering airline and travel-brand climate programs spanning credits, CDR and SAF
companies.signal: Powers programs for major airlines and brands like Lonely Planet; VC-backed (Gen Catalyst among investors)

companies.name: CNaught
companies.what: API selling pre-diversified, science-weighted carbon credit portfolios at a single price
companies.signal: Seed-stage; positions as the 'index fund' of carbon credits

companies.name: Wren
companies.what: Consumer climate-subscription app funding a vetted project portfolio
companies.signal: Tens of thousands of subscribers; YC-backed

companies.name: Ecologi
companies.what: UK consumer/SME climate subscriptions (trees + credits), expanding into footprint software
companies.signal: Tens of millions of trees funded; pivoted toward SME carbon tooling as consumer offsetting cooled

variations.name: Buyer-side procurement & credit portfolio management platforms
variations.description: Software and managed services that help corporate buyers screen, purchase, manage and retire credit portfolios across registries, replacing opaque broker-by-broker buying with data-driven procurement.

companies.name: CEEZER
companies.what: Berlin enterprise platform aggregating 3.5M+ data points to build and manage cross-registry credit portfolios
companies.signal: €10.3M Series A led by HV Capital (Jan 2024); 50+ corporate clients, 150+ developers

companies.name: Abatable
companies.what: Procurement intelligence and RFP marketplace; publishes VCM developer surveys and country policy rankings
companies.signal: ~$13.5M raised (2023); used by corporates and governments for sourcing diligence

companies.name: goodcarbon
companies.what: Berlin platform for nature-based credit portfolios with forward offtake structures
companies.signal: Seed/Series A-stage; focused on high-integrity nature portfolios

companies.name: South Pole
companies.what: World's largest carbon credit retailer/advisor managing corporate portfolios end-to-end
companies.signal: Hit by 2023 Kariba over-crediting scandal (CEO exit, layoffs) but continues operating globally

companies.name: ClimatePartner
companies.what: Munich full-service provider combining footprinting, credit portfolios and consumer-facing labels
companies.signal: Thousands of corporate clients across Europe

companies.name: 3Degrees
companies.what: US environmental-markets firm handling renewable energy and carbon credit procurement and portfolio advisory
companies.signal: Long-standing US corporate client base across RECs and carbon

companies.name: Salesforce Net Zero Marketplace
companies.what: Carbon credit marketplace embedded in Salesforce's Net Zero Cloud, powered by Cloverly
companies.signal: Launched Oct 2022; still listed as active but low public traction since launch

variations.name: CDR-specific procurement platforms & advance market commitments
variations.description: Dedicated buyer coalitions and marketplaces channel forward purchase commitments to early carbon-removal suppliers, providing the demand certainty engineered CDR needs to scale.

companies.name: Frontier
companies.what: Stripe-run advance market commitment pooling buyer funds (Alphabet, Shopify, Meta, McKinsey et al.) for durable CDR offtakes and prepurchases
companies.signal: >$1B in commitments toward 2030; the benchmark AMC for engineered removals

companies.name: Symbiosis Coalition
companies.what: Google/Meta/Microsoft/Salesforce AMC for high-integrity nature-based removals
companies.signal: Pledged 20M tonnes of nature-based removal credits by 2030 (launched May 2024)

companies.name: NextGen CDR Facility
companies.what: South Pole–Mitsubishi joint venture aggregating corporate demand for high-durability CDR at fixed prices
companies.signal: Targets ~1Mt of durable removals; buyers include major financial institutions

companies.name: Milkywire
companies.what: Runs the Climate Transformation Fund pooling corporate money (Klarna et al.) into vetted CDR and decarbonization portfolios
companies.signal: Multi-year corporate commitments; popular with tech brands as a Frontier alternative

companies.name: Supercritical
companies.what: CDR marketplace for tech companies that sources, contracts and guarantees delivery of removal tonnes
companies.signal: $13M Series A led by Lightspeed; new funding secured to expand supply development

companies.name: CUR8
companies.what: Removals intelligence and market-making platform building buyer portfolios and supplier finance access
companies.signal: $6.5M raised from Google Ventures and Airbus Ventures

companies.name: Carbonfuture
companies.what: CDR marketplace plus digital tracking (MRV+) platform, strongest in biochar supply chains
companies.signal: Series A-stage; trusted delivery layer for Microsoft and other large CDR buyers

companies.name: Terraset
companies.what: Nonprofit channeling philanthropic donations into durable CDR purchases
companies.signal: Small but growing donor base; complements corporate AMCs

companies.name: Nori
companies.what: Soil-carbon removal marketplace with blockchain-tracked retirement
companies.signal: Raised $17.25M over 7 years; shut down September 2024 citing stagnant VCM demand and funding drought

variations.name: Credit ratings & risk-scoring agencies
variations.description: Independent agencies score the integrity and over-crediting risk of individual credits and projects, giving buyers a quality signal the registries themselves don't provide — increasingly embedded in regulation and procurement.

companies.name: BeZero Carbon
companies.what: Largest ratings coverage on an 8-point scale; expanding into CORSIA and compliance-market ratings with AI-assisted workflows
companies.signal: $32M Series C (Jan 2025, led by GenZero with Japan Airlines); 100+ corporate subscribers; appointed to Singapore's NEA eligibility panel Nov 2025

companies.name: Sylvera
companies.what: ML- and geospatial-data-driven ratings plus market data; pushing toward 5,000 'estimated ratings' coverage
companies.signal: $57M Series B (Balderton, 2023; ~$96M total); appointed to Singapore's NEA ratings panel Nov 2025

companies.name: Calyx Global
companies.what: Independent ratings covering both GHG integrity and SDG impact across thousands of projects
companies.signal: Appointed alongside BeZero and Sylvera to Singapore's International Carbon Credit framework panel (Nov 2025)

companies.name: Renoster
companies.what: Deep-dive, openly published reviews of forest carbon projects used in pre-purchase diligence
companies.signal: Small specialist; publishes free ratings to pressure market transparency

companies.name: MSCI Carbon Markets (ex-Trove Research)
companies.what: Investor-grade VCM project quality scores, price forecasts and market analytics inside MSCI's data stack
companies.signal: Trove Research acquired by MSCI in late 2023 — the first major consolidation of carbon intelligence into mainstream financial data

companies.name: CarbonPlan
companies.what: Nonprofit publishing open-source data, offset databases and critiques of crediting methods
companies.signal: Influential watchdog whose analyses have triggered methodology reforms

variations.name: Carbon credit insurance & buffer-pool alternatives
variations.description: Insurers underwrite delivery failure, reversal, invalidation and political risk on carbon credits, replacing crude registry buffer pools with priced, capitalized risk transfer that unlocks institutional buying.

companies.name: Kita
companies.what: First Lloyd's coverholder dedicated to carbon: delivery-risk, reversal and non-payment insurance covers
companies.signal: Underwriting capacity up 450% to £22.5M for 2025, backed by Chaucer, Munich Re Specialty, RenaissanceRe and Tokio Marine Kiln

companies.name: Oka, The Carbon Insurance Company
companies.what: Lloyd's syndicate-in-a-box (launched Jan 2024) insuring post-issuance risks: invalidation, reversal and clawback
companies.signal: ~$10M seed (Aquiline); first syndicate dedicated to carbon credit risk

companies.name: CarbonPool
companies.what: Zurich insurer founded by ex-Allianz executives that pays claims in-kind with carbon credits — a capitalized buffer-pool replacement
companies.signal: $12M seed (Feb 2024) from climate-focused investors

companies.name: Howden
companies.what: Insurance broker that launched the first carbon credit invalidation cover (2022, with Respira and Nephila capacity) and brokers carbon covers globally
companies.signal: Multiple distinct carbon product categories now live across its book

companies.name: Chaucer
companies.what: Lloyd's (re)insurer providing underwriting capacity behind Kita's carbon policies since 2022
companies.signal: Part of the expanding reinsurance panel (with Munich Re Specialty, RenRe, TMK) backing carbon risk

variations.white_space: Total insured capacity (~tens of £M) is trivial versus a multi-billion-dollar market because actuarial loss data barely exists; openings include rated buffer-pool replacements at registry scale, Article 6 political-risk cover (only MIGA-style instruments exist), and portfolio-level covers that let pension-grade capital hold credits.

variations.name: Tokenized carbon & blockchain registry infrastructure
variations.description: Blockchain rails tokenize credits for transparent, fractional, programmable trading and settlement — a wave that crashed after registry bans and crypto winter, now rebuilding as registry-sanctioned digital infrastructure.

companies.name: Toucan Protocol
companies.what: Bridged 20M+ tonnes of credits on-chain and created the BCT/NCT liquidity pools; pivoted to registry-sanctioned tokenization after Verra's 2022 ban
companies.signal: Survived the crash; volumes a fraction of 2021-22 peak

companies.name: KlimaDAO
companies.what: DAO that accumulated millions of tokenized credits in its treasury and runs on-chain carbon liquidity/retirement
companies.signal: Activity far below 2021 peak; relaunched automated market infrastructure (Klima 2.0)

companies.name: Flowcarbon
companies.what: Adam Neumann-cofounded venture to tokenize nature-based credits via the Goddess Nature Token
companies.signal: Raised $70M (a16z-led, 2022); token never launched; quietly refunded investors and wound down by 2024

companies.name: Carbonplace
companies.what: Bank-built DLT settlement network (BNP Paribas, UBS, NatWest, Standard Chartered et al.) linking registries for instant credit transfer/retirement
companies.signal: $45M from nine global banks (2023); partnerships continuing into 2025 but transaction traction modest

companies.name: Moss.earth
companies.what: Brazilian issuer of the MCO2 token backed by Amazon forest credits
companies.signal: Little verifiable activity in 2024-26

companies.name: Thallo
companies.what: Built a two-way registry bridge and 'carbon-as-a-service' API for embedding tokenized credits
companies.signal: $2.5M raised (2022); no substantive public activity since 2024

companies.name: Regen Network
companies.what: Purpose-built blockchain and standard for on-chain ecological credits
companies.signal: Niche but operating; issues its own eco-credit classes

variations.white_space: Wave one died when Verra banned tokenization of retired credits (2022) and crypto liquidity evaporated — proving the registry, not the chain, is the choke point; the live opening is boring, registry-blessed infrastructure (digital custody, settlement, corresponding-adjustment tracking) sold to banks and registries rather than public token pools.

variations.name: Compliance market software & services (ETS allowance management, trading & cap-and-trade tooling)
variations.description: Brokers, auction platforms and software that help obligated emitters procure, hedge, manage and surrender allowances across the EU ETS, UK ETS and North American cap-and-trade programs.

companies.name: EEX (European Energy Exchange)
companies.what: Operates the EU ETS primary auctions on behalf of member states plus secondary derivatives and German national ETS sales
companies.signal: Core public infrastructure of the world's largest carbon market

companies.name: Vertis Environmental Finance
companies.what: Budapest-based EU ETS broker/advisor serving 1,000+ industrial emitters across Central/Eastern Europe
companies.signal: Voted Best Trading Company and Best OTC/spot Broker for EU ETS and UK ETS (Environmental Finance 2025 rankings); now an STX Group company

companies.name: ClearBlue Markets
companies.what: Carbon market advisory plus a market-intelligence platform spanning EU ETS and North American programs
companies.signal: Voted Best Advisory/Consultancy for both EU ETS and North America (Environmental Finance 2025)

companies.name: Redshaw Advisors
companies.what: Independent London carbon risk-management firm running hedging and buying programs for industrial compliance entities
companies.signal: Long-standing specialist desk for EUA/UKA procurement

companies.name: Homaio
companies.what: French fintech opening EU allowance (EUA/UKA) investment to individuals and smaller institutions
companies.signal: Seed-funded (2024); first retail-facing EUA investment platform

companies.name: IncubEx
companies.what: Designs and develops environmental futures/options products with Nodal Exchange (EEX group) for North American carbon and REC markets
companies.signal: Founded by the former Climate Exchange/CCX team; products live on Nodal

variations.white_space: Trading and brokerage are well served, but software is thin: EU ETS2 (from 2027) pulls tens of thousands of fuel suppliers and SMEs into compliance with no fit-for-purpose allowance-management SaaS — an opening analogous to what tax-compliance software did for VAT.

variations.name: Article 6 / sovereign carbon infrastructure
variations.description: Registries, meta-data layers and transaction services that let countries authorize, track and trade ITMOs under Paris Agreement Article 6 with corresponding adjustments — the plumbing of the emerging sovereign carbon market.

companies.name: KliK Foundation
companies.what: Swiss CO2-Act compliance buyer financing mitigation abroad and importing ITMOs for Switzerland's NDC
companies.signal: 22 new ITMO purchase agreements signed in 2025; received first-ever African ITMOs (11,733 from Ghana cookstoves, July 2025); expects ~CHF27/t average cost 2025-30

companies.name: UNDP (National Carbon Registry / Carbon Cooperation)
companies.what: Open-source national carbon registry software (an accredited Digital Public Good) plus an ITMO cooperation platform for host countries
companies.signal: Registry codebase informs infrastructure in 10+ countries with World Bank/UNFCCC/EBRD partners

companies.name: Climate Action Data Trust (CAD Trust)
companies.what: World Bank/IETA/Singapore-founded meta-registry harmonizing credit data across registries to prevent double counting
companies.signal: Data Model v2.0 consultation in 2025; v1.0 already baselines national registries in 10+ countries

companies.name: APX / Xpansiv Connect
companies.what: The registry-technology provider operating the back-end ledgers for multiple major crediting programs and environmental markets
companies.signal: Acquired by Xpansiv (2023), concentrating much of the market's registry infrastructure in one owner

companies.name: Perspectives Climate Group
companies.what: Specialist advisory structuring Article 6.2 frameworks and ITMO transactions for governments and buyers
companies.signal: Involved in the Swiss-led bilateral pilot ecosystem (Ghana, Vanuatu and others)

companies.name: Gold Standard (Article 6 services)
companies.what: Provides crediting, registry and authorization-tracking services adapted for Article 6 labelled units
companies.signal: Standard of choice for several first-mover Article 6.2 cookstove deals

variations.white_space: Almost no private companies exist here: infrastructure is built by UN bodies, the World Bank and consultancies, while first ITMOs only began flowing in 2024-25; as CORSIA Phase 1 demand collides with scarce authorized supply, there is an opening for ITMO transaction management, escrow/settlement, corresponding-adjustment tracking and sovereign-risk analytics as commercial SaaS.

variations.name: Market intelligence & price data providers
variations.description: Price reporting agencies, analytics firms and news services that create the reference prices, forecasts and transaction data an opaque, OTC-heavy market needs to function.

companies.name: Veyt
companies.what: Oslo analytics firm (ex-Point Carbon/Refinitiv team) covering EU ETS, UK ETS, North American and voluntary markets with price data and forecasts
companies.signal: Partnered with Carbon Pulse (Mar 2025); named Climate Risk Advisory Firm of the Year three years running

companies.name: AlliedOffsets
companies.what: Largest aggregated database of VCM projects, prices and transactions used by traders, researchers and governments
companies.signal: Tracks tens of thousands of projects across all major registries

companies.name: Quantum Commodity Intelligence
companies.what: Price reporting agency founded by ex-Platts/Argus staff publishing daily voluntary and CORSIA carbon assessments
companies.signal: Established PRA for VCM benchmarks alongside its oil/biofuels coverage

companies.name: Carbon Pulse
companies.what: Subscription newswire dedicated to carbon pricing, ETS policy and market intelligence
companies.signal: The de facto trade press of carbon markets; Veyt data partnership (2025)

companies.name: OPIS (Dow Jones)
companies.what: Publishes daily carbon price assessments across VCM, RGGI, California and global compliance markets
companies.signal: Part of Dow Jones since 2022, mainstreaming carbon price data distribution

companies.name: S&P Global Commodity Insights (Platts)
companies.what: Platts carbon assessments (CEC, CNC, etc.) extend the world's main energy PRA into carbon
companies.signal: Carbon benchmarks referenced in physical and derivative contracts

companies.name: Argus Media
companies.what: PRA publishing voluntary and compliance carbon assessments plus Article 6/ITMO cost analysis
companies.signal: Covers emerging sovereign carbon pricing (e.g., Swiss ITMO cost expectations)

companies.name: Ecosystem Marketplace
companies.what: Forest Trends nonprofit publishing the benchmark State of the Voluntary Carbon Markets transaction surveys since 2006
companies.signal: Its annual survey remains the most-cited VCM volume/price dataset

variations.name: Third-party validation & verification bodies (VVBs)
variations.description: Accredited auditors validate project designs and verify claimed emission reductions/removals before registries issue credits — the human assurance layer every credit depends on, and a chronic capacity bottleneck.

companies.name: DNV
companies.what: One of the largest global VVBs auditing projects across Verra, Gold Standard, CDM and Article 6 pipelines
companies.signal: Decades of accreditation across all major programs

companies.name: TÜV SÜD
companies.what: German certification giant with a major carbon validation/verification practice
companies.signal: Accredited across CDM and leading voluntary standards

companies.name: SCS Global Services
companies.what: US certifier verifying forestry and land-use carbon projects alongside its sustainability certification business
companies.signal: Long-standing VVB for North American forest carbon

companies.name: Earthood
companies.what: India-headquartered VVB that became one of the busiest auditors in the global VCM on cost and turnaround speed
companies.signal: Among the highest project-audit volumes of any VVB

companies.name: SustainCERT
companies.what: Gold Standard spinout repositioned as a digital-first VVB after GS changed its assurance model; also approved under ICR and Isometric
companies.signal: Raised $37M (2022); discontinued legacy GS certification services and re-approved as independent VVB in 2024-25

companies.name: Aster Global Environmental Solutions
companies.what: US specialist VVB focused on forestry/agriculture project audits
companies.signal: Niche but active across ACR/CAR/Verra projects

variations.white_space: Verification queues stretch many months because accreditation takes years and the auditor pool is tiny relative to project volume; ICVCM/CORSIA quality bars raise workloads further — an opening for dMRV-integrated, AI-assisted audit platforms that accredited bodies adopt, or for new VVBs purpose-built for digital registries like Isometric and Puro.
